text:
tony_valencia: @support urgent — Valencia Clinic is asking for evidence of access audit logs for a recent compliance review. They say patient-access events from 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-15 are missing. Ticket SUP-9221. They need proof of retention for HIPAA/BAA (7 years) or clear guidance on what we can provide.

eva_support: Thanks @tony_valencia. I'm pulling their account now (acct: valencia-clinic-prod). Can you confirm whether they're on Dedicated or Hosted? Also asked for the exact event IDs they expect.

leah_sales: They're on Hosted API (standard tier) but signed a healthcare addendum during onboarding — I attached the scanned addendum to SUP-9221. They expect audit-level retention guarantees.

samir_eng: Quick triage — do we have any backend errors around KMS decryption for audit log blobs in that timeframe? Search shows a couple of transient decrypt errors around 2026-03-13 02:14 UTC.

maya_security: @samir_eng can you paste the KMS error lines? We need CMK alias + request IDs for KMS logs to feed to AWS support / our HSM vendor if it's an HSM-backed key.

samir_eng: Pasting the snippets I found:
```
ERROR [audit-archiver] 2026-03-13T02:14:17Z - Failed to decrypt s3://redwood-audit/valencia/2026-03-13/part-0001.gz: KMS.DecryptError; KeyId: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345; RequestId: 5f7a2a4b-1a2b-4c3d-9e8f-11aa22bb33cc
WARN  [audit-archiver] 2026-03-13T02:14:20Z - retrying decrypt (attempt 2)
INFO  [audit-archiver] 2026-03-13T02:14:25Z - decrypt succeeded
```
Looks transient but coincides with missing entries the customer reports.

maya_security: That KeyId is our hosted CMK (not HSM). I'll pull KMS CloudTrail for that key and check for throttling or unusual denies. If this is transient, records should still be in S3; the archiver retried and succeeded — we need to confirm whether some objects were never archived due to earlier failures.

jon_oncall: I'm going to run the archive verification job for valencia-clinic-prod now. If anyone needs to reproduce locally, use:
```
# export audit logs range
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/logs?account=valencia-clinic-prod&start=2026-03-12T00:00:00Z&end=2026-03-16T00:00:00Z" -o valencia-audit.json
# expected 1.2M lines
```
tony_valencia: I ran that curl and got a 403 with body: `{\"error\":\"access_denied\", \"message\":\"Audit logs not enabled for account\"}` — which is weird because they explicitly requested audit logging during onboarding and we turned it on.

eva_support: 403 suggests a customer-level flag or misconfigured role. @samir_eng can you check the account config for "audit_enabled" and the IAM role used by the archiver? Also, attach the exact curl output to the ticket.

samir_eng: Checking tenant config: audit_enabled = true. Archiver IAM role looks fine. I see a skew where some shards failed S3 PUT with `AccessDenied` from a malformed bucket policy change on 2026-03-12 01:58 UTC. There was a deploy that changed lifecycle rules; deploy-bot shows that rollout.
\
deploy-bot: deploy started by @ci - change: infra/audit-lifecycle v2.1.3 -> v2.1.4; rollout completed to 60% at 2026-03-12T01:57:58Z.

samir_eng: After the lifecycle change, a bucket policy conditional accidentally blocked the archiver role for specific prefixes for ~12 minutes. Some objects returned 403 on PUT and were retried, others were skipped due to a bug in retry backoff. That explains partially missing files.

maya_security: This is sensitive. Even transient missing audit blobs could be a compliance issue. We need to: 1) enumerate which object prefixes were skipped, 2) reconstruct events from request logs and API traces (we may have event copies in request logs), 3) produce a remediation and communicate to the customer.

jon_oncall: I'm starting an immediate verification run to list S3 objects for the date range and compare counts against expected. Command I'm using:
```
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-audit/valencia/2026-03-13/ --recursive --human-readable > s3-listing.txt
python tools/audit_count_check.py s3-listing.txt expected_counts/valencia-2026-03-13.json
```
I'll paste diffs.

leah_sales: We should prepare a customer-facing statement. They asked for retention evidence. If we can't fully reconstruct, legal wants us to offer an attestation and next steps plus timeline for full recovery. @maya_security can you prepare recommended language for SUP-9221?

maya_security: Draft checklist for the customer:
- summary of incident (brief)
- what we checked (archiver logs, KMS decrypts, S3 lifecycle changes, retry logic)
- what we recovered (list of object ranges restored)
- what is still missing (if any) and why
- proposed mitigation (extend retention, re-run archiver, manual re-ingest from request logs)
- timeline and owner contacts

eva_support: Action items:
- eva_support -> coordinate recovery with customer and share initial statement (ETA 4h)
- jon_oncall -> full S3 listing + diff (ETA 2h)
- samir_eng -> run request-log reconstruction for 2026-03-12 01:40-02:20 UTC and output events (ETA 6h)
- maya_security -> legal phrasing and risk assessment (ETA 6h)
- leah_sales -> prep customer comms and contract implications (BAA addendum) (ETA 6h)

tony_valencia: Please mark this P1 — the clinic's auditors expect an update today. They're specifically asking whether we can guarantee 7-year retention for audit logs and whether KMS/HSM was used for those particular blobs.

maya_security: Short answers for now: we used hosted CMK (AWS KMS) for audit blob encryption during that period, not an HSM-backed key. Per their BAA, we need to confirm whether hosted CMKs meet their policy; if not, we need to discuss HSM-backed options under Private deployments. I'll flag legal.

samir_eng: One more repro note — if anyone needs to reproduce the 403 PUT from that deploy window, run a local archiver dry-run against the affected prefix; sample command:
```
python tools/archiver_dryrun.py --account valencia-clinic-prod --date 2026-03-13 --prefix audit/part-
# look for HTTP 403/AccessDenied lines
```

jon_oncall: Posting preliminary diff: missing 18 objects (~1.2% of that day's archive). I'm attaching the object keys to SUP-9221 (internal). Looks like a combination of PUT AccessDenied and a retry bug that gave up after 3 attempts.

eva_support: Thanks. I'll escalate to Legal + Account Exec. For the customer: give them an interim statement acknowledging the issue, confirming we are reconstructing events and offering a timeline for a full attestation.

leah_sales: I'll coordinate with the AE and draft the interim. If legal requires contract changes for HSM, that'll be an enterprise/private deployment conversation. Keep me in loop.

maya_security: I'll open an internal post-mortem + compliance ticket and include required artifacts for auditors (KMS CloudTrail export, S3 object listing, archiver logs, request-log reconstruction).

tony_valencia: Appreciated. Please include a copy of the archive verification output and the exact list of missing event IDs. Auditor will want hashes.

eva_support: Noted. Closing loop: SUP-9221 updated with owners and ETAs. I'll ping again when we have the reconstructed events. :eyes:

jon_oncall: I'll update in 30m with full S3 listing diff.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for infra/audit-lifecycle to v2.1.3 by @ci at 2026-03-13T03:05:12Z (safety rollback after detection).

maya_security: After rollback, archiver retries completed and new puts succeeded. We'll still need to remediate the 18 missing objects.

samir_eng: Plan B: reconstruct missing events from request logs -> re-run archiver ingest to produce synthetic blobs and upload them under a verified prefix `recovered/valencia/...` with manifest and checksums. Need approval for re-upload to production audit bucket.

eva_support: @maya_security and @leah_sales — please approve re-upload plan so we can present a single audit artifact to the customer.

maya_security: Approve the re-upload under `recovered/` prefixed, with manifest and signed checksum. Legal to sign off on wording.

leah_sales: Approved from AE side as long as we document chain of custody and provide checksums.

tony_valencia: Thanks all. Please Cc auditors once you have the attestation.

eva_support: Thread updated. SUP-9221 now has the S3 diffs, KMS CloudTrail request IDs, and the recovery plan. Follow-ups: I'll keep posting progress here.
